title: Settings Reconcile Selection
prompt: A React settings table keeps selected row ids, but filters can remove visible rows. Write a helper that keeps only selected ids still present in the rows array.

explanation.beginner:
Example: settingsReconcileSelection(["a","b","c"], [{"id":"a"},{"id":"c"}]) produces ["a","c"]. Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “removes missing ids”: input [["x"],[{"id":"a"}]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

The reference uses map, filter. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “removes missing ids”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
